correctness.rationale: For the literal half-turn involution, invariant independent sets correspond to independent orbit vertices after deleting any orbit containing an edge. Equal barycentric weights on each orbit give a PL homeomorphism of geometric fixed space to the quotient conflict graph independence complex; augmented signed trace is -I(Q_n;-1). Graph folding yields upper and lower A paths of combined length 2n+1, M path length n, and specified alternating cross edges. Exact eight-state layer transfer with odd A, even B and cap t yields I_n; an independently reconstructed integer matrix T=BA satisfied T^8−T^7+2T^6+T^4=0 entrywise, and the eight initial coefficients yielded the exact odd/even rational numerators. Therefore the all-n generating function follows algebraically, not from 15 samples; independent first fifteen terms matched. Denominator 1+z+z^4 has no unit-circle zero, product of root moduli one and no numerator cancellation, ensuring a root inside the unit disk and exponential coefficient limsup; recurrence and nonperiodicity follow.
residual_risks: No assertion of individual fixed-space Betti numbers or homotopy type beyond Euler trace.

value.rationale: Natural rotational symmetry of an already-studied width-two hexagonal independence-complex family produces an exact all-length alternating homology trace with surprising nonperiodic exponential growth; a reusable 8-state transfer provides a meaningful equivariant invariant neither fixed-space Betti ranks nor ordinary homotopy determine.
residual_risks: The fixed Euler character is meaningful by symmetry and contrast with non-equivariant work, not because any arbitrary short recurrence is publishable.

final_claim: For every n>=1, the reduced Euler characteristic of the geometric half-turn fixed points of the independence complex of the three-rail width-two hexagonal strip has generating function z^2(z-1)/(1+z+z^4), satisfies e_n=-e_{n-1}-e_{n-4}, and grows exponentially along a subsequence; it equals the reduced rational Lefschetz trace of the half-turn.
